author: internetleftovers
post:
Why don't I just DO the things I need to do to "feel better"? I have all the coping skills. I've received in-patient *and* out-patient treatment at a psychiatric hospital. I've been going to therapy for years. Still, I am here again. I feel this way again.

[Dysthymia, aka Persistent Depressive Disorder.](https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/persistent-depressive-disorder/symptoms-causes/syc-20350929) Most of the time, my depression is moderate enough that I can't even justify to myself why I don't just *do* the things I *know* I need to do to feel better. I literally have the tools. If the 10 days I spent in a psychiatric hospital taught me anything, it's that **daily structure, social interaction, and three meals a day** are the simple solutions to what I'm feeling right now. 

It's as if my brain is attached to inadequacy. It paints the world around me grey and opaque, and all I see are the signs that things aren't the way they are supposed to be. That my chunk of consciousness is seemingly broken or disabled. And that my unhappiness is a direct result of the things I avoid. And are, in a way, my doing and my fault.

The things I don't do to change my circumstances are so obvious. I don't feel pitiful as much as I feel fucking frustrated. When I get a foothold on my life, I look around me and see there is nowhere to put my hands. Before I can remind myself that *there* *is always a way up*, my body descends whatever mountain face it was climbing.

**Fear**. Am I just afraid? I know what *content* feels like. This rat race in my mind sends me running in circles, taking myself down just to pull myself up again. Am I addicted to this? Is living this way just a comfortable alternative to the scary risks and efforts of a fully-engaged life? And is it pointless to keep looking for a "cure"? That lock and key that will make things different? Does it exist? Or do I have to struggle this way forever, settling for a life as a functioning depressive?

Finding myself *here* again is like an anti-high. Like how people say taking LSD puts you in an indescribable brain-space that you only have access to when you are tripping. *This* is the opposite. I can't seem to access the parts of my brain that I feel when I'm *truly content,* now*.* And I'm frustrated because I know I have felt content before–and I know that space in my mind exists–so *why can't I access that brain-space now*.

I'm just ready and impatient to feel good again. I know what I need to do, so why don't I just ***do****?*

Depression is a distortion? I was watching a video on youtube and Mic the vegan was talking to Dr. Dean Ornish, never heard of him but the things he said about depression kinda hit me and I'd like to share.

"The worst thing about being depressed is that it's a true reality distortion field. You really think you are seeing things clearly for the first time, that things are bad, they have always been bad, they're always going to be bad. That's where that helplessness and hopelessness, which is the hallmark of depression really comes from. And it's a true distortion, that's where people start to think "well, if things are always gonna be bad, why don't I just do myself in?" It is a distortion and that's why it's important to reach out and try and get a different reality because it is a true reality distortion, its not the way things are"

"Often times depression comes because people think they have to get something outside themselves to be happy and be able to love themselves. "If only I had more money/power/beauty/sex/accomplishments, then I'd be happy" once you are set on this view of the world, however things turn out you feel more depressed because if you don't get it you feel bad, if someone else gets it then you feel really bad, and even if you get it it's good for a few moments and then it doesn't really fill that void "now what?/it's never enough/so what if I got it? Please Read. Thank You. ***Michael*** was never who you knew. None of you saw the real me. I was merely the image of what I perceived as ‘fun.’

Ever since I was a freshman in highschool I can remember being numb. I didn't feel anything, and i don't mean physically. I never felt attracted to anyone or cared about my "friends." This has left me alone in a cruel world. I have contemplated my own life many times before and it is always a terrible experience. I was so absorbed in these feeling of darkness, of this pitfall I had been thrown into at the hands of the demons I carry with me, that I was not even able to kill myself. If I am being completely honest, I wish I just had life taken from me. That is just my mind's way of pitying me.

I see my mind in a way I feel like people can relate too. Like a large house with many rooms all with their own locks. But those doors lock from the inside and if you're on the outside all you can do is wait for someone to open up. And when the doors open up, your greeted with one of two things. Someone like happiness, who is glowing and teeming with energy, energy I have not felt in years. The other option is the door opens and something awful walks out. Depression. Fear. Anxiety. These monsters terrorize the house as they overtake it simply by unlocking the door. The only reset is to go to sleep and hope the next day someone better will unlock their door. For three years not a single 'good feeling' has greeted me.

This is the life I lead. Day in and day out dragging my emotionless body off to school where people make jokes about how I look like a zombie, or how I have not slept. That is because there is no escape from the purest form of misery. Even when you sleep, which so many people see as their bliss, the way they escape their problems even for a little while is just another prison for me. This awful, dreadful existence is what I live every day. The thing is, nobody knows anything is wrong with me.

You may be wondering how would I be able to conceal such a terrible life? How can nobody know? My answer to you is the mask I wear. This mask portrays me as a fun-loving, energetic 16 year old kid who is perfectly contempt with the life he lives. I make jokes and I smile, I talk with my friends about their carefree, unimportant problems as I sit there behind my mask caging the demon within me that wants to yell out "PLEASE HELP ME! I AM TRAPPED IN A MONSTER!" You read that correctly. I think my demons are scared of me, see me as the true evil. They are scared of what I think, scared of how easily I suppress my real self and take on this polar opposite persona. See i'm the real monster here. And monsters do not deserve to live.

***I will not take my own life. I fear wherever I end up next will be worse. Worse than this personal hell.***

I do not ask for your advice. I do not ask for your pity. I only ask one thing of you. Compare your life too mine. How does yours seem now? Most of you will say not as bad. I made it this far. Why can't you?

***For the unfortunate souls who say their life is worse I have no advice, nothing to offer, and can only imagine what you must deal with. For that I solemnly apologize.***

author: sierra_p
post:
If you don’t feel like your diagnosis is right, don’t be afraid to get another opinion! I was diagnosed with mild anxiety and depression as a teenager, by my pediatrician. I was never referred to a specialist for medication/treatment. The diagnosis never seemed right, my symptoms were so much worse than “mild.” But the diagnosis never changed, no matter what I said to my doctor. 

I am now 21 and I finally saw a new doctor, who diagnosed me with major depressive disorder, generalized anxiety order, and post traumatic stress disorder. And then it was further explained to me how my treatment was mismanaged. 

My point here is that myself, like many others in this sub, accepted a diagnosis that didn’t fit. I have my reasons, and you have yours. But getting this new diagnosis that fits had been so beneficial for my health. Please, please, please, if something doesn’t feel right, try a new doctor, try a new opinion. Get the answer you deserve.
